newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan may cancel naphtha tender on high offers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may cancel naphtha tender on high offers.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it might cancel its heavy naphtha import tender for November delivery as the offers were too steep.
A CPC source said it would consider offers of $225-$230 per tonne, cost-and-freight basis, as "tolerable" but the offers it received were over $230.
The tender, which closed on October 8, sought 28,000 tonnes of heavy naphtha for November 11-30 delivery, c-and-f Kaohsiung.
Naphtha prices have been on an upswing recently and hit a five-year high in afternoon trade in Tokyo, the sixth consecutive day of rises, due to high crude prices.
Traders noted that the European market has also been strong.
In its previous tender, CPC bought 30,000 tonnes of heavy naphtha around $200 per tonne, for October 21-31 delivery, c-and-f Kaohsiung.
